title: Scarbound - Dust Road Groove (in-game loop)

sections.intent: groove from the first beat: riff, bass, drums with side stick, shaker
the motif (call), a slide answer, the motif up a third, its answer
the lift: snare and ride, strummed archtop, the road melody
the motif on the slide guitar, then only its falling tail; metal and wood percussion; the lead answers
calm: pad, ringing arpeggios, the call slowed down; drums rebuild in the last two bars
the high point: the motif with a second voice, the full band, the call reaches G5
back to the road texture; one slide accent; a light fill into bar 1

brief: Scarbound (mobile idle arcade RPG, wasteland road, Mustang pickup with a hood gun and a harpoon turret): the in-game background loop. Dusty western / desert blues groove, 100 BPM, 4/4, E minor (G-major pitch classes only), warm muted baritone riffs, sparse slide guitar, round bass, soft dry drums and shakers, wood and metal percussion, a delicate pad. Groove from the first second, a calm stretch and a return, 48 bars that loop without a seam.

association.whole: A battered Mustang pickup rolls out of a dusty garage onto the canyon road; the hunchback mechanic rides the bed behind his harpoon turret, the little hood gun ticks, scrap clinks in the back, the truck takes a ramp, the mesa opens up and the wasteland goes quiet for a moment before the road picks up again.

gives.what: the road: a riff that rises into beat 2 and leaves the rest of the bar to the drums; light sixteenth swing like wheels on washboard dirt
scrap and the garage: brake drum and anvil accents, a guiro scrape, slit drums; the harpoon turret as the slide guitar
canyon road, ramp and open mesa, back to the road: riff/theme, the open-road lift, a dust-quiet stretch, the return
the mesa opens: bVI-bIII-bVII-i (C G D Em) over the riff's E drone

plan.identity: a baritone riff on an open E that rises into beat 2 and leaves the bar's second half to the drums; a five-note call (B D | E . D B ... E) that starts in that space and slides into its high note; G-major pitch classes only

high_point.means: the call with a second voice, the full kit with snare and crash, strums, and the call's high variant reaching G5

sections.differs: the loop's first bar: groove at once, no melody
the call enters in the riff's space; ghost hats; a slide answer
C G D Em: the relative-major lift, a chord every bar, snare and ride, strums, the road melody
the motif moves to the slide guitar; brake drum, guiro, anvil; side stick again
no riff for six bars, pad and ringing arpeggios, the call in long notes; the drums rebuild in its last two bars
the motif with a second voice, snare backbeat, crash, strums
the ignition texture again, one slide accent, a light fill into bar 1

decisions: highpass:bass: 36 Hz keeps the E1 fundamental within about 2 dB and keeps sub-bass out of a phone game mix, as the brief asks.
highpass:riff: the baritone riff leaves its lowest fundamentals to the bass on purpose (a 70 Hz high-pass).
stiffness:pad: the pad is the delicate bed the brief asks for; its chords are held blocks under a moving band.
melody_velocities:slide: the slide guitar plays few, sparse accents; their shape is in the pitch bends.
Tempo 100 BPM: 48 bars = 115.2 s, an integer number of samples at 44.1 and 48 kHz, so the loop survives resampling to the game's 44.1 kHz without a fractional seam.
E minor with G-major pitch classes only: the G-major level-up and unlock fanfares sound over every chord.
Light sixteenth swing (0.57) on every part, bends placed at the swung positions.

The pad is the Surge XT patch juno_60_strings (a probe: 0.5 s swell, -40 dB 3.1 s after release, L/R correlation 0.59), low-passed at 6 kHz and narrowed to 0.6 width for mono phones; xenofish/pads/breeze was dropped (correlation 0.05, -2.8 dB in mono, a 13 s release that smeared the chords). The bass is mono below 120 Hz (mix.mono_below_hz).
Master at -17 LUFS integrated, true peak under -1 dBTP: the game plays music under engine, gun, harpoon and UI sounds.
loop_seam: the turnaround repeats the ignition texture (riff, bass, side-stick kit, shaker, low pad); its last bar is the D riff run and a light snare fill that land on the Em of bar 1.
loop_seam.timbre: the slide's last fall (bar 47) and the brake drum of bar 48 do not sound in the first second of bar 1; the riff, bass, kit, shaker and pad carry the seam.
outside_chord.melody: the melody is pentatonic over a drone-like riff; its unresolved ninths and sixths (E over D, B over C) are the colour of the style, as in rock and blues verses.
outside_chord.accompaniment: the same colours in the riff and the strums (Cadd9 shapes, the riff's sixth).
parallels: the bass and the riff double the last pickup into each downbeat at the octave on purpose.
low_intervals: the riff is a baritone part and sits above the bass by design; the pad was moved out of the low register (three upper chord tones) after the first review.
highpass:slide: 200 Hz keeps the slide's low B3 within 1.6 dB; the part is a thin, high accent.
highpass:comp: the comp's rare low notes (A2 in the dust arpeggio) are allowed to lose some weight.
